findings.title: Resumed-arm perf risk unmeasured at scale
findings.problem: Spec required a production-scale benchmark (or EXPLAIN ANALYZE) of the new resumed-session arm against a realistically sized `resumed` population, recorded before merge; only a qualitative, few-thousand-row check was run, and the doc's own proposed mitigation (extending `session_dims_active_shared_cov`'s INCLUDE list) was left undone, with just a TODO to re-measure later.
findings.impact: Arm 6 ("started, resumed") runs a per-row fenced probe across five tables for every resumed session; at the real ~1.9M-session scale the doc cites elsewhere, an unmeasured regression could slow every session-listing endpoint, with no fallback wired in.
findings.recommendation: Before merge, either run scripts/cli_analytics_bench/run_sessions_bench.py (or EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)) against a production-scale resumed population and record the numbers in cli-analytics-storage.md, or get an explicit human sign-off to ship without it and implement the INCLUDE-list fallback as a safety net.
findings.check_notes: fix_evidence maps artifacts + 4 commands (benchmark run, exit_code 0, doc updated) but no decision.outcome/rationale; kind=decision requires a recorded human decision, which is absent.

fix.change: Ran the production-scale benchmark (coordinator decision): seeded the disposable local Postgres with 1.9M session_dims rows (950K started-in-window baseline, 902.5K out-of-window filler) and swept the resumed cohort through 0/0.1%/1%/2% of the started-in-window population (half cheap, half expensive sub-case each), measuring scripts/cli_analytics_bench/run_sessions_bench.py latency at each size. Recorded the four measured points in cli-analytics-storage.md's 2026-11-12 entry and spec.md's Open Risks. Decision from the numbers: the budget (825ms) holds through 1% resumed and is crossed only past 2%, against the one real observed fraction (~0.001%, 100x below the in-budget 0.1% point) -- the INCLUDE-list fallback migration is NOT implemented. All seeded bench16496-* rows were deleted and the tables VACUUM (ANALYZE)d back to their pre-benchmark state.
fix.test: n/a (documentation + decision finding; proof is the recorded benchmark numbers and commands in code-review-fix-evidence.local.json)

findings.title: Ops reset script has no batching
findings.problem: The one-time `UPDATE session_dims` reset runs as a single, unbatched statement with four correlated NOT EXISTS subqueries over the full table, unlike RollupRefresher's batched refresh (batch_size=100) used elsewhere in this change.
findings.impact: At the ~10^6-row scale the accompanying doc describes (where a 30-day default page already times out), this risks a long lock/transaction or a statement timeout when the ops step is actually run.
findings.recommendation: Batch the UPDATE (e.g. by session_id range or a LIMIT-driven loop, mirroring RollupRefresher's batch_size pattern) instead of a single table-wide statement.
findings.check_notes: Script now loops in 5000-row batches with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED and a per-batch COMMIT, mirroring RollupRefresher's batch pattern.

fix.change: Batched the ops reset UPDATE into a DO block looping 5000-session batches (FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, committed per batch) instead of one table-wide statement.
fix.test: n/a (no existing/possible unit test for a standalone ops .sql script); syntax and effect verified by hand-running the script against a live Postgres schema (codemie_analytics) before/after seeding rows

findings.title: Reset script doesn't check lines_daily is zero
findings.problem: The script's comment says it targets sessions whose has_activity came "solely from a zero-value lines_daily row," but the WHERE clause only checks that a lines_daily row exists and no row exists in the other four activity tables — it never checks the lines_daily values are actually zero.
findings.impact: A session with genuine, nonzero lines-only activity is also reset to NULL and needlessly re-derived by the next backfill cycle, beyond what the script's own comment promises.
findings.recommendation: Add the same zero-value check reader.py uses elsewhere (e.g. `AND NOT (l.lines_added <> 0 OR l.lines_removed <> 0)`) to the lines_daily EXISTS clause so only genuinely zero-value rows are targeted.
findings.check_notes: lines_daily NOT EXISTS clause now requires lines_added <> 0 OR lines_removed <> 0, matching the comment's zero-value claim.

fix.change: Added a NOT EXISTS clause requiring every lines_daily row of the session to be zero-value, so a session with any genuine nonzero lines_daily row is no longer reset.
fix.test: n/a (no existing/possible unit test for a standalone ops .sql script); manually verified against a live Postgres schema: seeded one zero-lines-only session and one nonzero-lines session, ran the script, confirmed only the zero-lines-only session's has_activity was reset to NULL

findings.title: New .sql ops script missing license header
findings.problem: scripts/ops/epmcdme_16496_reset_zero_lines_has_activity.sql is a new source file with 13 non-empty lines; per scripts/license_headers/check_license_headers.py, .sql has a defined comment style and is not restricted by INCLUDE_PREFIXES or the 5-line too-small exemption, so it is eligible for the project's Apache 2.0 header, but carries none.
findings.impact: The file fails the project's own license-header gate (make license-check) as committed.
findings.recommendation: Run `make license-fix FILE=scripts/ops/epmcdme_16496_reset_zero_lines_has_activity.sql` or prepend the standard Apache 2.0 `--`-comment header.
findings.check_notes: Script now carries the standard Apache 2.0 header (lines 1-13).

fix.change: Added the standard Apache 2.0 `--`-comment license header via `make license-fix`.

findings.title: No seeded test for UTC-midnight hour presets
findings.problem: The spec's Testing section requires a semantic, seeded-row unit test for an hour-based preset window crossing UTC midnight, pinning that the partial day still needs a raw in-window record (not just a daily rollup row). Only a SQL-string-shape test (comparing generated CTE text to a hand-mirrored string) was added; no live-Postgres/seeded-row test exercises this scenario.
findings.impact: The pre-existing AND-join in `_active_in_window` that enforces this rule is pinned only by a string comparison, so a change that breaks the real query while still matching the mirrored string would not be caught by any test that actually runs the query against Postgres.
findings.recommendation: Add a live-Postgres seeded-row test in test_live_session_period_membership.py that seeds a daily-rollup-only session on a UTC-midnight-crossing hour-preset window's partial day and asserts it is excluded absent a raw in-window record.
findings.check_notes: New live-Postgres seeded test test_utc_midnight_crossing_hour_preset_excludes_daily_rollup_only_partial_day exercises the real AND-join, not a string comparison.

fix.change: Added a live-Postgres seeded-row test (test_utc_midnight_crossing_hour_preset_excludes_daily_rollup_only_partial_day) in test_live_session_period_membership.py: a daily-rollup-only session on a UTC-midnight-crossing hour-preset window's partial day is asserted excluded absent a raw in-window record, against an admitted control with activity inside the window's clock-time bounds.

findings.title: underived_started evaluates _live_resumed twice
findings.problem: `underived_started`'s OR of two branches calls `_live_resumed(a, True)` once in each branch, generating the same five-table, fenced EXISTS clause twice in the final SQL text instead of once.
findings.impact: Every candidate row in the "started, underived" arm (sessions whose has_activity/resumed facts aren't yet derived) pays for ten correlated EXISTS probes instead of five; this doubled cost has no corresponding benchmark entry, unlike arm 6's resumed-arm cost which the accompanying doc does track.
findings.recommendation: Compute `_live_resumed(a, True)` once into a local variable and reuse it in both branches of the OR.
findings.check_notes: underived_started now computes _live_resumed(a, True) once into a local var, reused in both OR branches (reader.py:346-348).

fix.change: Computed _live_resumed(a, True) once into a local variable and reused it in both branches of underived_started's OR, instead of generating the same five-table fenced EXISTS clause twice.
fix.test: poetry run pytest tests/codemie/repository/cli_analytics/postgres/test_reader.py -q (387 passed, generated SQL text unchanged)

findings.title: Underived-resumed admission arm never runs live
findings.problem: Arm 2 ("started, underived")'s resumed-aware branch — the new `_live_resumed`-driven logic that closes the EPMCDME-16993 reopened-session gap for sessions whose has_activity is still NULL — is only checked as a substring of generated SQL text. Every async test in test_live_session_period_membership.py calls `await _refresh(engine, ...)` before any admission assertion, so has_activity/resumed are always derived (non-NULL) by the time admission is checked, and this branch never executes against a real Postgres database with real seeded rows.
findings.impact: A logic or operator-precedence bug in how this branch combines `_live_resumed` with `_active_in_window`/`_has_any_activity` — or a real-Postgres NULL-handling edge case — would ship unnoticed for exactly the cohort this branch exists to handle: a session recently ingested but not yet picked up by the rollup refresher.
findings.recommendation: Add a live-Postgres test that seeds a resumed session's raw/rollup rows and runs the admission query without first calling _refresh/derive_session_activity, so has_activity/resumed stay NULL and the _live_resumed-driven branch actually executes, then assert the correct admit/exclude outcome.
findings.check_notes: New live test test_underived_resumed_session_decided_live_without_backfill deliberately skips _refresh so has_activity/resumed stay NULL, exercising the live branch for real.

fix.change: No code change (recommendation was test-only). Added a live-Postgres test (test_underived_resumed_session_decided_live_without_backfill) that writes session_dims and turns_daily rows directly, skipping _refresh/derive_session_activity, so has_activity/resumed stay NULL and the _live_resumed-driven branch of arm 2 ("started, underived") actually executes against real Postgres; asserts the correct admit/exclude outcome for a resumed-but-underived session with and without in-window activity.

final_round.rationale: The edge-case lens file was missing/unreadable so that lens failed this round, forcing confidence to low. Acceptance flagged 4 unmet spec/testing requirements (no ticket for the Cursor coverage gap, no production-scale resumed-arm benchmark, and two missing live-Postgres seeded-row tests, one for the brand-new underived-resumed admission path) and standards flagged a blocking missing license header on the new ops script; together with two correctness/robustness issues in that script and a redundant SQL-generation call, these yield 2 decision_needed items and 6 patch findings. 3 blind-lens claims (an undefined-looking constant, an unverified command_name assumption, an unconfirmed variable-arity consumer) were checked against source and dismissed as false positives; nothing was deferred.
